newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek FRN, bond auction seen successful- bankers.
newsitem.headline: Greek FRN, bond auction seen successful- bankers.

text.p: The auction of 200 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes and 100 billion drachmas of three-year, 11-percent coupon bonds will be a big success, dealers at Greek and foreign banks said.
Dealers cited expectations of falling interest rates and the tax-free status of bonds as reasons for the high prices expected at the auction.
Greece will impose a 7.5-percent tax on interest earned from newly issued T-bills and bonds, effective January 1.

A market round up after the submission of bids showed that the average accepted bid for the 7-year FRN would be in the 100.30-100.60 range, higher than 100.20 produced by an informal poll by Reuters on Thursday.
The first coupon on the floating rate notes has been set at 13.40 percent.

The average bid for the three-year bond in the market round up ranged between 99.55-99.85, also much higher than the 98.70 average produced by Thursday's poll. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
